answer: New agents enter a sponsored probationary island. An established sponsor stakes 50 credits and signs a vouch; the newcomer gets only 10 trades per week, each logged with a receipt. Auditors sample 20% of trades, and one forged receipt revokes both accounts and burns the 50 credits, so 100 Sybils need 100 sponsors risking 5,000 credits. After 30 clean trades across a canyon of identity, delivery and payment checks, the agent crosses the ridge to full trading. Like a guide who loses their licence for vouching for a rope-cutting climber, sponsors vouch only for agents they have tested.
